sources.entry: Flipt - Feature flag solution with support for multiple data backends (alternative to LaunchDarkly). (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Docker/K8S/Go

summary.one_liner: Flipt is a self-hostable feature flag platform that stores flag configuration in Git repositories, with a single-binary server and optional Pro features.
summary.what_it_does: Flipt v2 is a feature management platform that stores flags as files in Git repositories, so changes have full Git history, blame, and diffs and can go through branches. It supports mapping environments to Git branches, directories, or repositories, with each environment having its own namespaces and flags. The server runs as a single binary and can be started locally or via Docker, with a web UI and a YAML configuration file. It exposes REST and gRPC APIs, supports Server-Sent Events for pushing flag updates to clients, and offers client-side local evaluation and OpenFeature/OFREP support. Secrets can be loaded from file-based providers in the open-source edition, while Vault, cloud secret managers, GPG signing, and merge proposals are described as Pro features.
use_cases: Manage feature flags alongside application code in Git
Roll out features to a percentage of users
Toggle features on and off without redeploying
Run a self-hosted alternative to a hosted feature flag service
Keep flag data inside your own infrastructure
Evaluate flags from client SDKs via OpenFeature
notable: Git-native storage: flags live in your own Git repositories with history and blame
Environments can map to Git branches, directories, or repositories
Zero external dependencies by default, shipped as a single binary
Server-Sent Events streaming for flag updates without polling
OpenFeature and OFREP support for vendor-neutral evaluation
caveats: GPG commit signing, merge proposals, Vault and cloud secrets integrations, and SCM PR automation are Pro features requiring a paid or trial license
Pro pricing is $200/month or $2,000/year; trial includes up to 5 instances
Some Pro items such as enterprise auth and advanced analytics are marked as coming soon
Server code is under the Fair Core License, not an OSI-approved open source license, though the awesome-selfhosted listing says GPL-3.0
summary.license: Server code: Fair Core License, Version 1.0, MIT Future License; client code and Go SDK (rpc/): MIT. README does not name GPL-3.0.
